pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Golden Values and Pledge
Muswell Hill is underpinned by the values:
To our pupils we pledge:
At Muswell Hill Primary School, the staff and governors are working every day so that by the time you leave us:

Welcome
Message from our Headteacher, Mandi
Welcome to Muswell Hill Primary School.
We are a happy, ambitious, high-achieving and inclusive school, reflecting the rich diversity of families in our area. I can’t imagine a nicer place to work.
I am proud and delighted to be the head of Muswell Hill.
At Muswell Hill, every child is encouraged to discover and nurture their interests and talents through a stimulating curriculum that has global dimensions, going beyond the basic national curriculum requirements.
We have a dynamic team of vocational teachers and teaching partners who act as exemplary role models, educating and nurturing each child, enabling them to achieve high standards of academic attainment, while enabling them to become capable, caring and confident human beings.
Alongside our hard working, dedicated and highly trained staff is a whole community of parents and carers drawn from a wide variety of backgrounds and cultures, each contributing to our learning environment and the school’s creative ethos.
Muswell Hill Primary School is set in beautiful grounds next to Alexander Palace. We have a modern, light and spacious building and a recently converted STEaM classroom. We also have excellent play and sports facilities adding to the range of our provision.
Muswell Hill Primary School is a two-form community primary school situated in North London. We are commited to the Rights of the Child and are passionate about young people’s learning. We relish the challenge of guiding them through the early stages of their lives.
The culture of our school ensures that every child is known well and valued. We are a happy, ambitious and inclusive school reflecting the rich diversity of families in our area. It is a safe and stimulating environment for learning, playing and growing.
Muswell Hill is a rights respecting community, which promotes active, global citizenship. We have an energetic and enthusiastic pupil voice, developed by a purposeful curriculum. This champions the rights of learners and provides an effective learning environment. We build individuals' capacity to collaborate, to transform themselves, their communities, and the wider world.
We work collaboratively across a professional Network Learning Community within Muswell Hill and Highgate, and across Haringey. This helps to develop pedagogy, curriculum and innovation for everyone, through training, research and evidence-informed practice.
In addition to our academic focus, we emphasise creativity, with a spotlight on performing and visual arts. We offer an enriched curriculum where the children’s heritage is valued and celebrated.
Our expansive Physical Education and games provision champions inclusive practice, while offering the opportunity to compete at a high level. We are proud to have achieved sporting success both locally and regionally.
The physical and mental well-being of all our children are equally valued, with prominence in the curriculum for both. We are committed to high quality outdoor learning within our amazing grounds.
We are very proud of our children and the team who help them thrive. We welcome all children, families and staff who share our vision and values. We encourage any prospective families to visit us and experience our community first hand. We look forward to meeting you!
Thank you for visiting our website. Navigate the pages to discover more about our wonderful school. Click here to find out how to book a tour.
We would like to thank Kate Kuzminova and Sarfraz Ali, two of our wonderful parents who took the photographs for our website. They willingly gave of their time and professional expertise to take the photos and then gave them to us for use on the website -we are really grateful and suggest you have a little search for them on the search engine of your choice!

pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - Wrap Around Care & School Activity Clubs
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care & School Activity Clubs
Wrap Around Care - Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club costs £6.50 a session (i.e. each day) and runs from 7.45am - 8.55am when children will be taken to their classes. Breakfast is served until 8.30am - a selection of cereals, toast and yogurt is served. The Breakfast Club is managed by Elaine Mason.
Wrap Around Care - MASC (Muswell After-School Club)
MASC costs £15.00 a session (i.e. each evening) and runs from the end of the school day until 6.00pm. A snack is served - generally a sandwich or a wrap. The club is managed by Darrell Gunter. Please note there are specific collection times for MASC - please speak to the office on application.
General information about our Wrap Around Care Provision
Following on from a Community Review around MASC and Breakfast Club. Places are allocated on an annual basis - one full school year. Both working parents and single working parents will be prioritised and 10 places will be reserved for vulnerable children each night, with 3 remaining emergency places each night. If you have accepted a place at MASC and do not attend - you will still be charged for every session.
NB: Parents and Carers will be asked to reapply over half term of Summer 1 (end of May/June bank holiday) and places will be allocated by the end of the first week back so parents have three months to adapt any childcare arrangements ready for the start of the new school year.
Applications for both Breakfast Club and MASC should be made by emailing Darrell Gunter at the School Office email address office@muswell-hill.haringey.sch.uk
Late collection charges: 6.00pm – 6.30pm £30.00.
Please note any late collection charges will be added to your account to cover the additional staffing costs to the school up to 30 minutes. Following this, safeguarding procedures will be followed in line with LA guidance.
After-school Activity Clubs
Information about after-school activities for the Autumn Term (starting September 2026) are available by clicking here. After school activities start the week beginning Monday 14 September 2026. Please check dates as some clubs start later in the term.
All school run clubs must be paid up by the last day of the half term (approximately 5-6 weeks to pay in full). If clubs are not paid for by this date the child/family will not be prioritised for the same club the following term.

pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - School Day & Uniform Expectations
pageCache.text:
School Day & Uniform Expectations
School Day
The school gates open at 8.50am and children in Years 1 to 6 must be in their classes promptly for 8.55am registration. The school day for Years 1 to 6 finishes at 3.25pm. Children in Reception (after their three-week settling in period) should register by 8.55am and pick-up time is 3.20pm. The total time per week is 32.5 hours (less 25 minutes for Reception).
School Uniform
These are available to buy at the start of the academic year and cost £5.00. Obviously, the children can wear these whenever they want to, but we do ask that they wear them for school trips (makes them easier to find!) and for class photos or as requested. Our Parent Staff Association (PSA) often sell second-hand school t-shirts at summer and winter fairs.
Although we are a no-uniform school we do ask that children wear appropriate clothing to school, for example, no cropped tops or tops with thin straps, no t-shirts with political logos, sensible footwear - no flipflops and only sandals with ankle support and covered toes. If in doubt do please ask.
Jewellery should not be worn unless they are small stud earrings. Jewellery should not be worn for PE lessons.
Children should not wear make-up to school.
Reception - red
Year 1 - orange
Year 2 - yellow
Year 3 - green
Year 4 - light blue
Year 5 - navy blue
Year 6 – purple

pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - Parent/Carer Useful Information
pageCache.text:
Parents/Carers Useful Information
We are proud of our wonderfully diverse and talented community of parents and carers and are delighted with the engagement they show in both supporting their children in their learning and the school in our efforts to provide engaging and creative learning opportunities.
When a child starts school here we ask all parents/carers and children to read and sign our Mutual Home/School Learning Agreement which outlines what we will do for your child(ren) and what we, in turn, would like you to do to support us. You can see a copy of this agreement here.
We hope that you will find the practical information we have provided in our Parent and Carer Handbook useful. If we have missed anything out, please do give us feedback - we want to include the sort of information that you find helpful.
We have just added a Haringey resource on screentime for Under 5s which you may find helpful here.
We have a long and comprehensive Communications Policy; a summary sheet for parents and carers is available here.
Mandi's 14 November 2025 Community Presentation is available here for those of you who couldn't make it to school in person.
Mandi presented our new 3-year plan to parents and carers on 3 February 2025- a copy of the presentation can be found here.
There are also some useful links to School Performance Data and Financial Benchmarking Information, as well as to Parent View here.
We hope that if you have any concerns about the school and/or your children that you will come and have a chat with us and that we will be able to help with any issues you may have. If however, your concern remains unresolved please see a Parents' Guide to School Complaints here. This guide has been produced as a collaboration between Parentkind, the DfE, Ofsted and Parent Friendly Schools and is designed to help you resolve concerns quickly, easily and positively with your school.
If you would like a paper copy of any of the information on the website, we can do this for you free of charge. Please contact the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - School Meals
pageCache.text:
School Meals
School Meals are provided by our caterers, Compass (incorporating Pabulum). With effect from September 2023 the Mayor of London agreed that all Primary School Children will be entitled to a free school meal.
Our lunch breaks are staggered to ensure every child has as long as they need to eat their lunch. The lunch hall is well supervised by members of staff and a member of the Senior Leadership Team is always on duty. The staff encourage the children to make healthy choices and behave well.
Every day the children are offered a choice of three main meals, including a vegetarian option. The children are also offered a selection of two cooked vegetables and can choose freely from the salad bar. The children have a choice of puddings, including fresh fruit and yogurt (made fresh in the school). We are a water only school (although milk may be offered to Reception children). We encourage collective responsibility by asking the children to clear their own plates when they have finished eating.
The 2026 menu can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Muswell Hill Primary School - Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Education (PHSE)
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Education (PHSE)
At Muswell Hill Primary School through PSHE and Citizenship we support children to be healthy and safe, make good friendships, be responsible citizens and prepare themselves for the next stage in their education and their role within society as responsible adults.
The British values are interwoven into the curriculum.
At Muswell Hill Primary School we use the Camden Scheme for the teaching of PSHE and Citizenship. Activities taught encourage children to make informed choices about a healthier and safer lifestyle: we prepare them to play an active role as a citizen, to forge good relationships and respect each other. Each year group has a focus on mental health to help children stay positive and know what to do when they find things challenging. The Camden Scheme also incorporates SEAL (Social and Emotional Aspects of Learning).
Through assemblies, Rights Respecting School articles and SEAL themes is introduced and explored every half term across the school both in the class and at assemblies.
We use drama/role play, stories and visuals to support teaching of PSHE/Citizenship and to simulate relevant discussions and to encourage children to understand and think from different people’s perspectives as well as their own.
Each class also have discussions through Circle time or use their Well-being Wednesday time. This creates a safe environment to allow pupils to talk about subjects like worries, manners, how to deal with a falling out and what makes us happy. The children will listen to each other and give positive feedback as well as ideas of how to tackle issues. This helps build their understanding of others, empathy and problem solving. Through circle time we can turn negatives into positives.
For details of our Relationship and Health Education Policy and Curriculum please see here and for the PHSE Curriculum Map 2025-26 see here.

Music
We are delighted to have been awarded the Music Mark of recognition for dedication and improvement because at Muswell Hill Primary School we recognise the importance of Music as a form of creativity and ensure that it is firmly embedded in our Music curriculum, which can be viewed here.
Our aim is that our children have access to range of music, and the opportunity to explore how it is created. A key part of the curriculum and integral to the development of Music in school is that children have the opportunity to create their own music, learn to sing and play musical instruments. See Music Development Plan 25-27 here.
Music is a subject that is celebrated and enjoyed by all children across the school. Muswell Hill Primary School is extremely proud of its two choirs and orchestra who perform on many occasions at school, across Haringey, and even at the Royal Albert Hall during the bi-annual Haringey Music Festival.
Our teachers deliver universal music lessons based on a highly structured learning sequence. The school encourages and enables children to pursue their own talents through learning how to play a musical instrument. As part of the Wider Opportunities Fund, each child in Year 4 learns the classical guitar, and we have guitar 'continuers' in both Years 5 and 6. Year 5 children supplement their knowledge of classical music by working with Apollo Music throughout the year. Through the school’s links with Haringey Music, children can be signposted to opportunities within and beyond the school that they can pursue to develop their talents further-with the opportunity to learn to play many other instruments.
We have after-school opportunities for children to write their own songs. The school holds a ‘Music Night’ twice a year where any child can perform on the night to a public audience. This has gained momentum and has become a favourite in the school calendar, hence twice a year opportunities. Children also perform at community events such as the PSA Summer and Winter Fairs.
In line with the national curriculum 2014, the curriculum at MHPS aims to ensure that all pupils: https://www.gov.uk/national-curriculum/key-stage-1-and-2

Art and Design
At Muswell Hill Primary School we believe and value creativity.
We recognise the importance of inspiring and engaging children to be curious about art and design. Our aim is to support our children in developing their experience of high-quality teaching and learning of art and design.
To support teaching, we use the Kapow Primary’s Art and Design scheme of work which aims to nurture pupils’ creativity, imagination and visual literacy, encouraging them to think like artists and designers. The intention is for pupils to develop the confidence to experiment, express ideas and communicate meaning through visual and tactile media.
The scheme promotes an appreciation of art as a powerful form of human expression, helping pupils to understand its role across different cultures, time periods and creative industries. It encourages children to value originality, take creative risks and reflect critically on their own work and that of others.
Kapow Primary’s Art and Design curriculum is structured around five strands that run through each unit:
These strands ensure a balanced coverage of the practical, theoretical and disciplinary knowledge pupils need to progress in Art and Design, while supporting the development of both creative confidence and critical thinking.
Kapow Primary’s Art and Design scheme of work covers the statutory guidance from EYFS (Reception) through to KS1 and KS2.
Each unit of the scheme covers specific content and aims of the Art and Design National curriculum. This ensures that every lesson contributes to a spiral progression of skills and knowledge, leading to the attainment of end-of-key-stage targets.
For EYFS, it details alignment with Early Learning Goals and Development Matters statements, providing transition and EYFS Art guidance.
We take every opportunity possible to showcase children’s work and hold an exhibition each year, taking on varying forms and have strong links with Alexandra Palace, PATN Haringey Arts network and Outreach at St Martins.
Over the past four years we have held events such as ‘A night at the exhibition’, ‘Fashion through the decades – including a whole school recycled fashion show’ linking sustainability to textiles to the history of costume. We held a ‘Sing me a picture exhibition’ linking music composition to seven focused artists from a range of genres. Our choirs composed seven original songs linked to the seven artists. All coming together for one incredible installation and performance.
This Spring (2026) we will be exhibiting our whole school project, ‘Photography as Living Archives’. At its heart, the project emphasises co-creation: teachers and pupils working together with artists, histories, and ideas to generate new meanings.
Photography becomes a living archive — not simply a record of the past, but a portal for exploring identity, memory, protest, and authorship. Working with an artist in resident, this is a DepART project supported by Haringey Creates and is a partnership born out of their initiative Creative Conversations to bring creative partners together. https://haringeycreates.com/
Our curriculum has been reviewed to ensure we study relevant artists who are local, rich in diversity and from across the globe over history. In Key Stage 2 some of our art aligns with other areas of our Humanities curriculum.
In line with the national curriculum 2014, the curriculum at MHPS aims to ensure that all pupils: https://www.gov.uk/national-curriculum/key-stage-1-and-2

Computing
At Muswell Hill Primary School, we believe that Computing (and digital literacy) are an essential part of the curriculum; subjects that should not only stand-alone but should be an integral part of all learning. Our curriculum can be viewed here.
Computing, in general, is a significant part of everyone’s daily life and children should be at the forefront of new technology, with a thirst for learning what is outthere. Computing within schools can therefore provide a wealth of learning opportunities and transferable skills explicitly within the Computing lesson and across other curriculum subjects.
Through the study of Computing, children will be able to develop a wide range of knowledge and understanding alongside fundamental skills that will equip them for the rest of their life. Computers and technology are such a part of everyday life that our children would be at a disadvantage would they not be exposed to a thorough and robust Computing curriculum. Our 21st Century children live in a time where there are many future employment opportunities within the broad scope of ‘technology’, and they must be taught knowledge, skills and ways of thinking that will enable them to participate effectively and safely in the digital world beyond our gates.
